newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone army battles hunters for eastern town.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone army battles hunters for eastern town.

text.p: The Sierra Leone army battled a militia of local hunters for control of the eastern town of Kenema on Sunday and bodies littered the streets, military sources in the town said.
The sources said the death toll was at least 10, but that it was unclear how many people had been killed in the part of town held by the hunters, known as Kamajors.

"Many people, especially civilians, have been killed in the battle and their bodies are lying about in the streets of the town," said one military source in Kenema, 200 km (125 miles) from the capital Freetown.
The sources said fighting began on Saturday, but had intensified on Sunday with the two sides trading rocket propelled grenades and heavy machinegun fire.
Several buildings were set ablaze by stray fire while the streets were deserted except for fighters, the sources said.
There is traditional rivalry between the two groups who fought together against rebels of the Revolutionary United Front but the cause of the latest clash was not clear.

"Senior government and military officers have been sent to the town this morning by President Tejan Kabbah to try to stop the fighting and to resolve the dispute which sparked off the fighting," army Chief of Staff Colonel James Max Kanaga told Reuters in Freetown.
Aid agencies in the capital said helicopters were being sent to evacuate their workers from Kenema. They did not say how the helicopters would be able to land if fighting continued.

"The intensity of the fighting has prevented us from leaving our quarters and going into the streets. We are evacuating all our staff with the exception of three who can treat the wounded when the fighting eventually dies down," the head of one aid agency said in Freetown.
He said thousands of civilians had fled Kenema to take refuge in nearby forests.
A peace deal between Tejan Kabbah and rebel leader Foday Sankoh was signed in November to try and end the civil war which erupted in 1991.
But implementation of the deal has dragged, threatening to unravel the peace process.
